Q24744408.label: 2016–17 Haitian Senate election
Q24744408.summary: Senate elections were held in Haiti with a first round on 20 November 2016, and a second on 29 January 2017. The first round was held simultaneously with the presidential elections and the second round of the parliamentary elections that still had a run-off pending in some constituencies since 2015.

Q3587544.label: 1968 French Senate election
Q3587544.summary: The fourth senatorial elections of the Fifth Republic were held in France on September 22, 1968.

Q164312.label: Antonín Švehla
Q164312.desc: member of Czech council and Czechoslovak politician (1873-1933)
Q164312.summary: Antonín Švehla was a Czechoslovak politician. He served three terms as the Interior Minister and three terms as the prime minister of Czechoslovakia. He is regarded as one of the most important political figures of the First Czechoslovak Republic; he was the leader of the Agrarian Party, which was dominant within the Pětka, which was largely his own invention. Švehla is also credited with the slogan of the Pětka: "We have agreed that we will agree."

Party: Republican Party of Agricultural and Smallholder People
Positions held: member of the Revolutionary National Assembly of Czechoslovakia

Q110453720.label: 2022 Serbian parliamentary election
Q110453720.summary: General elections were held in Serbia on 3 April 2022 to elect both the president of Serbia and members of the National Assembly. Initially, parliamentary elections were scheduled to be held in 2024; however, in October 2020 president Aleksandar Vučić said that snap parliamentary elections would be held in or before April 2022.

Q117661656.label: June 2024 Bulgarian parliamentary election
Q117661656.summary: Early parliamentary elections were held in Bulgaria on 9 June 2024, to elect members of the National Assembly. The election coincided with the European Parliament election on the same day.

Q1330136.label: Second Battle of Fallujah
Q1330136.desc: Late 2004 battle of the Iraq War
Q1330136.summary: The Second Battle of Fallujah, initially codenamed Operation Phantom Fury, Operation al-Fajr was an American-led offensive of the Iraq War that began on 7 November 2004 and lasted about six weeks.

mentions.c: Iraq: Battle: Second Battle of Fallujah

Q891864.label: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
Q891864.summary: The Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing occurred on the night of 20 September 2008, when a dumper truck filled with explosives was detonated in front of the Marriott Hotel in the Pakistani capital Islamabad, killing at least 54 people, injuring at least 266 and leaving a 60 ft (18 m) wide, 20 ft (6.1 m) deep crater outside the hotel.

mentions.c: Pakistan: Terrorist attack: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing

Q1818072.label: Maersk Alabama hijacking
Q1818072.img: Surveillance photo of Maersk Alabama lifeboat, hijacked by pirates 090409-N-0000X-926.jpg
Q1818072.summary: On 8 April 2009, four pirates in the Somali Basin seized the Danish/U.S. cargo ship Maersk Alabama at a distance of 240 nautical miles southeast of Eyl, Somalia. The siege ended after a rescue effort by the United States Navy on 12 April. At the time of the hijacking, Maersk Alabama was owned by the Danish shipping company Maersk Line.

Q14944216.label: 2013 Balochistan earthquakes
Q14944216.desc: earthquake to the north-northeast of Awaran in Balochistan, Pakistan
Q14944216.summary: The 2013 Balochistan earthquakes were the deadliest to affect Pakistan since 2005. The mainshock, occurring on 24 September, had a moment magnitude of 7.8 and maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). It had an epicenter located in Awaran District, 113 km (70 mi) northwest of Bela.

Q853976.label: First Battle of Ypres
Q853976.desc: 1914 First World War battle fought for the strategic town of Ypres
Q853976.summary: The First Battle of Ypres was a battle of the First World War, fought on the Western Front around Ypres, in West Flanders, Belgium. The battle was part of the First Battle of Flanders, in which German, French, Belgian armies and the British Expeditionary Force (BEF) fought from Arras in France to Nieuwpoort (Nieuport) on the Belgian coast, from 10 October to mid-November. The battles at Ypres began at the end of the Race to the Sea, reciprocal attempts by the German and Franco-British armies to advance past the northern flank of their opponents.

Participants: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

Q132568.label: Battle of the Somme
Q132568.desc: battle of the Western Front, World War I
Q132568.img: British Mark I male tank Somme 25 September 1916.jpg
Q132568.summary: The Battle of the Somme, also known as the Somme offensive, was a battle of the First World War fought by the armies of the British Empire and the French Republic against the German Empire. It took place between 1 July and 18 November 1916 on both sides of the upper reaches of the river Somme in France. The battle was intended to hasten a victory for the Allies. More than three million men fought in the battle, of whom more than one million were either wounded or killed, making it one of the deadliest battles in human history.

Q38872.label: Prussia
Q38872.desc: common term for the Duchy, the Kingdom and the Free State of Prussia (1525–1947)
Q38872.summary: Prussia was a German state centred on the North European Plain. It originated from the 1525 secularization act of the Prussian part of the State of the Teutonic Order. For centuries, the House of Hohenzollern ruled Prussia, expanding its size with the Prussian Army. Prussia, with its capital at Königsberg and then, when it became the Kingdom of Prussia in 1701, Berlin, decisively shaped the history of Germany. Prussia formed the German Empire when it united the German states in 1871.

Q2135512.label: Austrian nationalism
Q2135512.summary: Austrian nationalism is the nationalism that asserts that Austrians are a nation and promotes the cultural unity of Austrians. Austrian nationalism originally developed as a cultural nationalism that emphasized a Catholic religious identity. This in turn led to its opposition to unification with Protestant-majority Prussia, something that was perceived as a potential threat to the Catholic core of Austrian national identity. It was also used to protect the rule of the Habsburgs.

Q11663832.label: Kakushin Club
Q11663832.summary: The Kakushin Club was a political party in Japan.
